text:
Rain was tapping at the tall windows of the reading room when I asked the archivist where it all began. She did not point to a plaque or a portrait. She pointed to a drawer.

Inside lies the Quillfeather Charter of Establishment, signed by Rosalind Tavner and filed with the Merrowdene Civic Records Office. It names Tavner as the founder of the Quillfeather Archive, and its authority is not in doubt. Desmond Okafor-Hale, Registrar of the Merrowdene Historical Society, certified the founding record, which was formally entered on 14 March 1987.

Tavner began with 2,300 donated manuscripts and pamphlets, a modest hoard by the standards of today's shelves. Yet every great collection has a first drawer, and this one belongs to her. Looking at the faded signature, one senses how much patience a single decision can set in motion.
